chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Malik ibn Ahmad ibn Harun narrated to us. He said: Ammar ibn Raja' narrated to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Amr informed us, from Abi Salama, from Abi Hurayra.

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, was approached by a man who said: O Messenger of Allah! Did you see how so-and-so travelled the sea with just a few goods and went to China, quickly returned, and came back with great gains, until his very friends envied him, and he was generous to his relatives and neighbours? So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Surely, whenever the wealth of this world increases in quantity and greatness, its owner increases in trial. So do not envy the people of wealth, except for one who is generous with his wealth in the way of Allah. But shall I not inform you of one who carries even fewer goods than your companion, who returns faster than him, who has greater spoils, and whose goodly things are preserved for him in the treasuries of the Throne of the Merciful? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah.

So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Look to the one who is coming toward you. So we looked, and behold, a man from the Ansar with a shabby appearance. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Today, this person has ascended to the heights of good deeds and acts of obedience, such that if they were divided among all the people of the heavens and the earth, the least of them would still have his sins forgiven and Paradise would be obligatory for him. They said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? So he said: Ask him to inform you of what he did today. So the companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, went to him and said to him: Congratulations to you over the glad tidings that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, has given regarding you. So what have you done today so that such can be written for you?

So the man said: I do not know what I did special today, except that I left my house seeking a need that I had been delayed in pursuing. I feared that I had missed it, so I said to myself: I shall certainly compensate for it by looking at the face of Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, for I have heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, saying: Looking at the face of Ali is worship. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: Yes, by Allah, it is worship, and what worship! O servant of Allah! You went out seeking to earn a dinar for the sustenance of your family, but it escaped you. So you compensated for it by looking at the face of Ali. You are a lover of him and a believer in his virtue. That is better for you than if the entire world were yours as a nugget of pure gold and you spent it in the way of Allah. And you shall surely intercede for every breath you took on your way to him, and Allah will free one thousand people from the Fire through your intercession.

key_terms.النَّظَرُ إِلَى وَجْهِ عَلِيٍّ عِبَادَةٌ: Looking at the face of Ali is worship - a famous prophetic saying affirming the spiritual merit of gazing upon the Imam
key_terms.بَلَاءً: trial/tribulation - the inherent test that comes with increasing worldly wealth
key_terms.خَزَائِنِ عَرْشِ الرَّحْمَنِ: the treasuries of the Throne of the Merciful - the stored spiritual rewards in the divine realm
key_terms.شَفَاعَة: intercession - the privilege of interceding on behalf of others on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about looking at the face of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain going back to Abu Hurayra, recounts a remarkable encounter where a man told the Prophet Muhammad about a merchant who prospered from a trip to China. The Prophet used this as an opportunity to teach that worldly wealth brings trials and pointed instead to a shabby-looking Ansari man as possessing far greater spiritual wealth. When questioned, the man revealed he had simply decided to look at Ali ibn Abi Talib's face as compensation for a missed errand, having heard the Prophet say that looking at Ali's face is worship. The Prophet confirmed this emphatically, declaring that this act was better than spending the entire world's worth of gold in God's path, and that the man would be granted intercession for a thousand souls freed from the Fire.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Qasim al-Astarabadi (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Abd al-Malik b. Ahmad b. Harun narrated to us. He said: `Ammar b. Raja’ narrated to us. He said: Yazid b. Harun narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Amr informed us from Abi Salama from Abi Hurayra. He said: `Ammar b. Raja’ narrated to us. He said: Yazid b. Harun narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Amr informed us from Abi Salama from Abi Hurayra.

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (s) and said: O Messenger of Allah! Did you see how so-and-so travelled the sea with just a few things, went to China, went quickly around the globe, and returned with great spoils, so much so that his relatives envied him, so it was distributed among his relatives and his neighbours? So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Surely, whenever the wealth of this world increases in quantity and greatness, its owner increases in trial. So, do not glamourize the people of wealth, except for one who is generous with his wealth in the way of Allah. However, shall I not inform you of one who carries even fewer things than your companion, who travels faster than him, who has greater spoils, and who has goodly things preserved for him in the treasuries of the Throne of the Merciful? They said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah.

So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Look to the one who is coming toward you. So, they looked, and they found a man from the Ansar with a shabby appearance. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Today, this person has climbed to the highest of goodness and obedience – if you were to divide it among the people of the heavens and the Earth, then the least of them would still have had his sins forgiven and Paradise would be obligatory for him. They said: Why, O Messenger of Allah? So, he said: Ask him to inform you of what he did today. So, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (s) went to him and said to him: Congratulations to you over the glad tidings that the Messenger of Allah has given regarding you. What have you done today so that such can be recorded for you?

So, the man said: I do not know what I did [special] today, except that I left my house seeking a need that I have been slow with. I feared that I had missed out on it, so I said to myself, “I will make up for it by looking at the face of `Ali b. Abi Talib (as)”, for I have heard the Messenger of Allah (s) say: “Looking at the face of `Ali is worship.” So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Yes, by Allah, it is worship, yes, it is worship! O servant of Allah! You went out to gain a gold coin to support your family, but you missed out on that. So, you made up for it by looking at the face of `Ali. You are a lover of him, and you believe in his virtue. That is better for you than having the whole world in pure gold and spending it in the way of Allah. You will be able to intercede for every breath that you take, and Allah will free one thousand people from the Fire through your intercession.
